To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the perception of modern risky technology is related to the behavioral immune system and that this is especially true for women.
people who perceive themselves more vulnerable to diseases are more negative toward GM foods, but females are more negative toward them.

1) the perception of modern risky technology is associated with disease-threat model; 2) the behavioural immune system is more activated by modern risky technologies possessing potential health hazards; and 3) the behavioural immune systems are activated especially when these technologies are associated with pathogen threat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the behavioural immune system in shaping attitudes toward risky technologies.
the evolutionary origins of the negative attitudes toward GM foods and the behavioural immune system.
the evolutionary origins and adaptive functions of the behavioural immune system, which is activated by disease-connoting stimuli, and the implications of this system in modern environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the acceptance of GM products is not a simple matter of the benefits of the products versus their perceived risks.
the behavioural immune system is a powerful predictor of attitudes toward GM products in the modern world.
the acceptance of modern risky technologies is associated with a lower perception of disease threat, but not with the expected reproductive goals, engaging in risky behaviour or food neophobia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
disease-threat model is a useful model for predicting attitudes toward GM products.
the disease-threat model is a good explanation for acceptance of GM products.
the disease-threat model explains acceptance or rejection of modern risky technologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the behavioural immune system can be used as a model to explain acceptance of modern technologies and products.
people with stronger behavioural immune systems are less likely to accept GM products.
we should be more careful in using GM products and that more information should be provided on the health risks of GM products.
